items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I recorded with Gerald Wilson in 1965.

ctx.x: But the musicians you mentioned from that period, your contemporaries from that period, who didn’t, you know, the record business changed, the scene changed, I’ve noticed that many of them have become educators and teachers. So, how did that come about?

Well, that was the next thing. We got the college situation happening, and many musicians who were capable of being able to express what they do to students and teach students, were the ones who then started to look at that and say, “Well, since I’m not working and there are fewer and fewer jazz clubs across the United States, let me do this.” So, there are a number of people all over the United States that started to teach. Many times, they were teaching as they were playing. Out in California, the musicians who…
What are the other four? (Laughs) You said there were five!
